body:
Context: `adlc-prosecute record-cross-model --ticket <id> ...` accepts any string as the ticket id. A typo'd id is accepted silently, writes a signed attestation bound to a ticket that has never existed, and prints success. Observed (issue #485): the 2026-08-10 forest cutover (#482) sealed the standing approves, and the census permanently contains BOTH `T-01KZGT27XA6C767VRP1T32Z60` (typo, missing `N`, recorded during the publish-order work) and `T-01KZGT27XAN6C767VRP1T32Z60` (the real ticket). The typo cost a duplicate distinct-provider review-and-record cycle at the time — the gate correctly refused to match it to the intended ticket — and the manifest is append-only, so the mistaken entry is permanent. #370 covered the sibling defect in the same record path (unsigned attestation written silently); this is the same accepts-garbage-and-reports-success class, one field over.

Build (all in packages/prosecute):
1. In `bin/adlc-prosecute.mjs`'s `record-cross-model` dispatch, immediately after the `--ticket` presence check and BEFORE the signing-key refusal, the revision resolution, and both write branches: resolve the repository ticket store and validate that `--ticket` names an existing ticket id. The check must gate BOTH write paths — the fresh-record path and the `--carry-forward` path — since both bind the appended entry to `--ticket`.
2. Store resolution must reuse the same fail-closed backend detection the tier path in this file already uses (`detectTicketStore` with `env: {}` and the repo root): a genuinely ABSENT store (the repo has no adlc ticket store at all) means there is nothing to validate against — print a one-line note and proceed, so downstream repos that use record-cross-model without a ticket store are unaffected; a store that EXISTS but cannot be resolved (ambiguous dual store, corrupt shard, unfinished migration) is an operational error: exit 1, nothing written.
3. Unknown id with a store present: exit 2, nothing written. The message must name the rejected id, state that it does not exist in the ticket store, list near-miss store ids when any are close (the recorded incident pair differs by one dropped character — a suggestion mechanism that surfaces `T-01KZGT27XAN6C767VRP1T32Z60` when given `T-01KZGT27XA6C767VRP1T32Z60` is the bar), and name the escape hatch flag.
4. Add an `--allow-unknown-ticket` boolean flag (default false) that skips the existence check. The historical seal census legitimately contains store-external ids (`359`, `140`, `431` — GitHub-issue-number-style references that are not store tickets); the flag is the deliberate, auditable path for those. Zero dependencies — the suggestion heuristic is hand-rolled (edit distance or prefix based), consistent with the package's dependency policy.
5. Update the help text: both `record-cross-model` usage forms document `--allow-unknown-ticket`, and the exit-codes section reflects that an unknown ticket id is a refusal (2), store-resolution failure an operational error (1).

Acceptance criteria (each verified by an automated test under packages/prosecute/test/, following the existing fixture-repo pattern in prosecute-cross-model-cli.test.mjs / helpers.mjs; failure-path exit codes asserted exactly, not merely non-zero):
- AC1 unknown id refuses without writing: in a fixture repo whose store contains ticket T1 only, `record-cross-model --ticket T-DOES-NOT-EXIST ... --allow-unsigned` exits 2, the manifest gains no entry, and the message names the rejected id and `--allow-unknown-ticket`.
- AC2 near-miss suggestion: fixture store containing `T-01KZGT27XAN6C767VRP1T32Z60`; recording with `--ticket T-01KZGT27XA6C767VRP1T32Z60` exits 2 and the message contains the real id as a suggestion.
- AC3 escape hatch: the AC1 command with `--allow-unknown-ticket` added succeeds and appends an entry bound to the given id.
- AC4 known ids are unaffected: recording with `--ticket T1` (no new flag) succeeds exactly as before.
- AC5 absent store: in a fixture repo with no ticket store, recording without the flag succeeds (the note line is printed).
- AC6 unresolvable store fails operationally: a fixture with BOTH a legacy `.adlc/tickets.json` and a directory store (the ambiguous-dual-store shape) exits 1 and writes nothing.
- AC7 carry-forward is gated too: `record-cross-model --ticket <unknown> --carry-forward <rev>` exits 2 before any chain inspection (message identical in kind to AC1).
- AC8 help: `adlc-prosecute --help` output names `--allow-unknown-ticket` in the record-cross-model usage.

Out of scope: cleaning up or annotating the historical typo'd entry (the manifest is append-only and the cutover seal is signed history); validating ticket ids anywhere other than the record-cross-model dispatch (tier-check and the gate read ids they are given; their matching semantics are unchanged); changes to the ticket-store packages themselves.
title: record-cross-model must fail closed on a ticket id absent from the store
